message: Skill default sends every test-typed task to a TERMINAL wave and, at fast tier, SKIPS the test coverage-gap sweep. Not applied here: this backlog has three test-typed tasks that are not coverage sweeps. T-1 is the kotlin.test convention-plugin wiring and MUST run first (testing.md: zero tests exist; nothing can compile a test before it lands). T-2 is the WCAG contrast sweep, the centerpiece of the Stage 2 gate decision. T-12 is the inspection-evidence pass. Applying the terminal-wave/skip heuristic literally would run the test infrastructure last and drop the contrast sweep entirely. Following the human-approved backlog executionPlan graph instead. Docs sweep trimming at fast tier is moot: T-13 is already a verified no-op.

Pre-execution baseline: ./gradlew :presentation-core-styling:compileKotlinDesktop :presentation-core-ui:compileKotlinDesktop BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 10s on host JDK 27 with jvmToolchain(21). Any later compile failure is attributable to this stage, not pre-existing.

.claude/rules/mappers.md documents ThemePreferenceMapper.toModel as defaulting to ThemeModel.Light. T-9 flipped that fallback to ThemeModel.System, so the rule file is now stale. The executor correctly did NOT edit a project rules file on its own authority. This staleness was introduced BY this spec and must be fixed before the spec closes - routing to the terminal wave rather than leaving it for Stage 5 to catch.

Batched T-4,T-5,T-6,T-7 into ONE worktree/agent instead of four sequential single-task waves. implementBatch=wave would spawn four agents for what is one cohesive organism build-up in a single module (atom/stage -> toolbar/statusbar -> side panel -> RectifyWindowShell assembling all three). T-7 assembles exactly what T-4/5/6 produce, so four agents would each re-read the same design screenshots, kit inventory and rules - 4x context reload for one unit of work, with a real risk of incoherent seams between layers. Dependency order is preserved INSIDE the agent (strict post-order). Scope is identical to the union of the four tasks predictedScope. Per-task reports and status are still emitted separately, so Stage 5 traceability is unaffected.

Stage 5 regression caught a REAL repo-wide defect this spec introduced: three commonTest backtick function names contained a comma/apostrophe, illegal on Kotlin/Native. Desktop compiled fine so the per-task green was honest but incomplete; compileTestKotlinIosArm64 and IosSimulatorArm64 failed, breaking ./gradlew build for the whole repo. Fixed in all three files; iOS test compile, desktop suite (44 tests) and four full module builds across every target now green. Note the plan explicitly specified the Stage 5 command as the four desktopTest tasks and warned against ./gradlew check because it builds Android/iOS for zero benefit - that guidance is right for the acceptance gate, but the broader build is what surfaced this, so it earned its keep as a non-regression check.

AC-34 CLOSED by direct human verification: the operator dragged the window edge and confirmed it stops at 1024x700. Traffic-lights-inside-the-toolbar and both-theme rendering were closed earlier by operator screenshots, measured against design comp 02 (green light right edge 68pt both, gap to first control 34pt both, Resolve & Send pill right edge within 1pt). SF Pro decision: keep Roboto Flex; the AC text references a typeface that has never existed in this repo - recorded as an AC-text discrepancy, not chased.

Operator granted full autonomy for the remainder of the chain: decide at every human gate without asking, finish app-shell-window-layout, then work down the portfolio deliverable by deliverable in dependency order until all are done. Policy adopted: take the agent-recommended option at each gate, record it in survey[] with source=orchestrator-auto and the rationale, and surface rather than silently absorb anything that (a) contradicts an earlier human-made decision, (b) is irreversible beyond a branch merge, or (c) is a genuine product/scope fork with no defensible default. Three further design comps supplied and cached to .pipeline/flow/design/: 03-device-picker-first-run, 04-error-adb-not-on-path, 05-error-no-device-detected - these belong to android-device-discovery-mirroring and error-handling-and-recovery.

Topological build order resolved from the PRD handoff feature graph. After app-shell-window-layout (F-1): 1 android-device-discovery-mirroring (F-2), 2 drag-annotate-frozen-frame (F-4), 3 error-handling-and-recovery (F-3), 4 measure-mode (F-5), 5 payload-preview (F-6), 6 resolve-and-send-mcp (F-7), 7 history-batch-tracking (F-8), 8 verify-and-rediff-loop (F-9), 9 ios-platform-support (F-10, priority=could). NOTE for when F-10 is reached: ios-platform-support directly contradicts NFR-10 (v1 is macOS only; the PRD itself labels it v1.1+). That is a product-scope fork with no defensible default, so it is one of the few things to surface rather than auto-decide. Each spec runs sdd-flow-prepare-input then the full 7-stage pipeline at --fast.
